title: Delta adds new nonstop service from Salt Lake City to Flagstaff, gateway to Arizona’s iconic outdoor destinations
summary: New twice-daily, year-round service beginning June 7, 2027, gives Salt Lake City customers convenient access to Flagstaff, Sedona and the Grand Canyon. |
body_markdown:
Delta is giving customers in Salt Lake City a new way to explore the American Southwest with the launch of nonstop service to Flagstaff, Arizona (FLG), beginning June 7, 2027.


## **A new gateway to the Southwest**


The new route will operate twice daily, year-round, providing convenient access to Flagstaff, known for its year-round outdoor recreation, vibrant historic downtown and some of the country's best stargazing.


The mountain destination also serves as a natural starting point for some of Arizona’s most iconic destinations, including the dramatic red rocks of Sedona, approximately 50 minutes away, and the South Rim of the Grand Canyon, approximately 90 minutes away.


Flights will be operated by Delta Connection carrier SkyWest Airlines on the CRJ-550, featuring a premium configuration designed to provide customers with an elevated regional travel experience.


## **More ways to connect through Salt Lake City**


Flagstaff is the latest addition to Delta’s growing Salt Lake City network, connecting customers to some of the West’s most sought-after destinations. The new service joins recently announced nonstop flights to Santa Rosa/Sonoma County (STS), launching Oct. 6, and Monterey (MRY), launching Dec. 19.


Delta is SLC’s largest global premium carrier, operating more flights from the airport than all other carriers combined, with 270 peak-day departures to more than 100 destinations around the world, including Amsterdam, London, Paris and Seoul.


SLC features two Delta Sky Clubs, including the nearly 34,000-square-foot Club in Concourse B, which opened in 2025 and is the second-largest in Delta’s network. The space accommodates up to 600 guests and features panoramic airfield views, a wrap-around premium bar and design elements inspired by Utah’s natural landscape.
